name: Smart Alert Co-Pilot
description: Move from 'checking on a schedule' to 'getting told the moment something's wrong.' An AI judgment layer watches your client records, pulls related context before deciding, and sends a targeted alert to the right person only when a change is actually worth interrupting someone for. (No instant Airtable-update trigger exists yet, so this polls every 10 minutes instead of firing immediately.)

notes.what: Works like an alarm clock — runs your workflow automatically at a specific time you set each day
notes.overview: Runs your workflow automatically on a schedule using a simple time picker. Select your time (HH:MM format) and timezone, and the workflow will execute daily at that time. Great for daily reports, periodic checks, or recurring tasks.
tips: Use 24-hour format (e.g., 09:00 for 9 AM, 14:30 for 2:30 PM)
Select your timezone from the dropdown (IST, UTC, etc.)
Workflow runs daily at the specified time
Test with manual trigger first
Timezone conversion is handled automatically
notes.why: Polls every 10 minutes because there is no 'row changed' trigger. One record per run.

notes.what: Reads rows from an Airtable base or adds new records — like a smarter spreadsheet
notes.overview: List, get, create, update, upsert, and delete Airtable records. The resource dropdown is visual only; runtime implements record operations, not table-management APIs.
tips: Use a Personal Access Token with data.records scopes or a saved Airtable connection
Base ID plus table/tableId are required for every operation
Create/update/upsert return records/count
Upsert also returns created and updated counts
Delete returns deletedRecords/count, not top-level deleted:true
notes.why: Picks up one record modified since it was last examined.

notes.what: Writes and runs any JavaScript you like to transform or process your data
notes.overview: Run sandboxed JavaScript once against the current workflow data and return the transformed value for downstream nodes.
tips: Always return the value the next node should receive
Default timeout is 5000ms and runtime caps at 30000ms
Use Output Schema such as {"type":"object"} only as a top-level shape hint
JavaScript has no credentials; connect downstream service node accounts separately
Do not paste API keys, tokens, or passwords into code
notes.why: Prepares the changed record for the AI to judge.

config.systemPrompt: You are a compliance monitoring co-pilot. You are given a changed client record plus related context records. Decide whether this change is worth interrupting a person for right now (e.g. a readiness score dropped sharply, a document expired, a risk flag appeared) versus routine (e.g. a timestamp update, a minor note edit). Reply as JSON: {"alertWorthy": true/false, "reason": "...", "severity": "low|medium|high"}.

notes.what: An autonomous AI brain that reasons, makes decisions, and uses tools on your behalf
notes.overview: Runs one prompt-driven AI step. The runtime extracts userInput from this node or upstream message-like fields, infers the provider from Model, calls the LLM adapter, and packages response_text plus optional structured fields.
notes.why: The judgment layer, and the reason this template exists: it decides whether a change is worth interrupting a person for, rather than alerting on everything.

notes.why: Sends high-severity alerts to the compliance lead and everything else to the account manager. Set both numbers here.

notes.what: Sends WhatsApp messages to customers via the official WhatsApp Business API
notes.overview: Send WhatsApp messages, media, locations, contact cards, approved templates, and interactive buttons/lists through the WhatsApp Business Cloud API. Connect a WhatsApp/Facebook account under Connections â€” credentials are resolved automatically. The visual panel exposes the Message resource; Contact, Conversation, Template, Campaign, and AI Agent resources are runtime-supported for advanced or AI-generated workflows.
tips: Connect a WhatsApp account under Connections â€” no access tokens entered on the node itself
Phone numbers should be in E.164 format, e.g. +12345678900
First message to a new contact must use Send Template; free-form Send Text only works inside the 24-hour customer service window
notes.why: Delivers the alert to the one person who needs it.

notes.why: Extracts the verdict, reason and severity from the agent's reply.

notes.what: Makes a yes/no decision: if something is true, go one way; otherwise go another
notes.overview: Makes a yes/no decision from previous-step data and routes matching work through TRUE and non-matching work through FALSE.
tips: Use the builder for normal setup; use JSON mode only when pasting prepared condition objects.
Choose AND when every row must match; choose OR when any row can match.
Use equals for statuses and categories, greater-than operators for numeric thresholds, and contains for text or lists.
Connect both TRUE and FALSE outputs so no business case silently disappears.
notes.why: Enforces the agent's verdict. Without this node the workflow alerts on every change and becomes a noisier version of a dumb alert.

Delete returns deletedRecords/count, not top-level deleted:true
notes.why: Stamps the record as examined — deliberately BEFORE the gate below, so records judged not worth alerting are not re-judged and re-billed on every subsequent poll.
